Subject: Migration options follow-up — quick context and constraints

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick note to capture the constraints we mentioned and to make sure we're aligned on the right migration path. We're HelixAI (NLP-driven clinical summarization) and currently running models on an in-house GPU cluster (mixed 2080/RTX A5000 hosts) and a small self-hosted Triton setup for inference. Two key drivers: (1) we need predictable tail latency for live triage (95th < 400ms target) and (2) strict data residency — PHI-scrubbed data remains in our VPC but audit logs/auditors will want proof of control.

Options we're considering after the call:
- Move to Redwood Hosted API for velocity (quick integration but need assurances on data handling and latency).
- Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation (sounds promising but need procurement/contract timeline and cost model).
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) if we must keep everything inside our network and manage keys.

Open questions for you:
1) How long does a Dedicated onboarding typically take (prod traffic day-one)?
2) For Private VPC, what networking patterns do customers use (transit vs private peering) and is there an air-gapped option?
3) Migration lift plan from Triton: do you have recommendations for model conversion/serving compatibility or is a parallel run advised?

I've attached our migration worksheet with current QPS, p95 latencies, and a sample payload size. Priya (cc'd) is our platform lead — she's the procurement point.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform — HelixAI

Alex — thanks for the clear doc and for outlining the constraints. Short summary from our side and proposed next steps so we have a working record:

Summary (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest pilot. Good for getting immediate latency wins with our edge routing and prefix caching but will require a brief assessment for PHI handling and an RTP (data processing addendum).
- Dedicated: recommended if you want predictable p95 latency and throughput with tenant isolation. Typical path is a reservation + staging pool and then a prod carve out.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): necessary if auditors require customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integration. We have both VPC peering and Transit Gateway patterns; fully air-gapped on-prem deployments are an engineering project but supported under enterprise engagements.

Answers to your questions:
1) Dedicated onboarding: median 4–6 weeks from signed order to prod capacity for teams that have models ready and basic networking in place. If you need end-to-end model onboarding (conversion + quantization), budget +2–3 weeks.
2) Networking patterns: most customers use AWS TransitGateway for multi-AZ isolation; large enterprises prefer private VPC peering with SAML + private link for the control plane. We can support static IPs for allowlisting and a managed connector for audit logs. Air-gapped on-prem takes longer (6–10 weeks) and requires an on-site packaging cycle.
3) Migration from Triton: parallel-run recommended. We provide an evaluation harness and a conversion checklist — common work is model format (TorchScript/ONNX), kv-cache warming, and latency tuning (sequence length profiling).

Proposed next steps:
- I will loop in Jordan for a short cost vs time proposal (Hosted vs Dedicated) and Naomi for SRE/networking scoping.
- If you can grant us a short window (1h) with your platform team next week, we can map an onboarding plan and a tentative timeline.

Action items:
- Alex/Priya: please confirm availability for a 1h scoping call (Mon/Tue next week) and attach any additional compliance docs.
- Vivek/Jordan: prepare a two-tier estimate (pilot on Hosted w/ fall-forward to Dedicated vs direct Dedicated onboarding).
- Naomi/Karthik: prepare a short note on peering patterns and required artifacts for procurement (SOC2 evidence bundle, certs).

I'll attach a short Dedicated pricing snapshot (baseline) for initial orientation — see attachment.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni

Alex — quick tech note from SRE to help you with the call prep:

1) Latency targets: for a 95th < 400ms target we typically recommend either Dedicated with pinned GPU pools or Hosted with an autoscaling policy tuned for low tail latency (min replicas + prewarmed kernels). If your request mix includes many cold-start short requests, Dedicated usually gives tighter control.

2) KV cache and prefix warming: if you're using session-based context, we can mirror KV caches during a parallel run. That reduces cold p95 significantly. We'll need a sample of typical session lengths and cache hit expectations.

3) Audit logs + evidence: we can provide streaming audit logs to your S3 (encrypted) and supply SOC2 artifacts and access logs. For Private VPC we can also integrate with a customer-managed KMS (HSM) — requires an architecture call to pin network flows and firewall rules.

I'll come prepared with a 1-page checklist for the scoping call that lists the networking artifacts and security docs you should have ready (IP ranges, PKI, expected egress, expected model sizes).

—Naomi
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
